Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

nestedscales 0.3.0

Breaking changes

  • New vocabulary, with no deprecated aliases: a member is one item of a frame (was “unit”), a leaf is a member of the finest layer and one row of the leaftable (was “atom”), and the leaf column is the column of the leaftable that identifies the leaves (was “key”). “Unit” now means a unit of measure only (unit_of_measure, from_unit, to_unit), and key= the column of a data table that holds the codes.
  • Renamed functions: scale_units() to scale_members(), scale_key() to scale_leaf_column(), scale_atom_level() to scale_leaf_frame(), recast_to_atoms() and recast_from_atoms() to recast_to_leaves() and recast_from_leaves(), product_atoms() to product_leaves(), scale_atom_pairs() to scale_leaf_pairs(), as_scale_unit() and is_scale_unit() to as_scale_member() and is_scale_member() (class scale_member). Renamed arguments: unit to member in filter_scale(), filter_product(), scale_children(), scale_parents(), scale_descendants(), scale_ancestors() and recast_crosswalk(); units to members in scale_label(); scale_units to scale_members in scale_distance(), cluster_scale(), cluster_contiguous() and cluster_sweep(); key to leaf in NestedScale() and scale_from_leaftable(). The property NestedScale@key is @leaf, and scale_vocab() returns member, members and leaves.
  • The label, alias and attribute tables, and the results of scale_labels(), scale_aliases(), scale_attributes(), scale_match(), scale_descendants() and scale_ancestors(), name the code column member (was unit); origin_unit is origin_member. scale_catalog() returns leaf and n_leaves (were key and n_atoms), summary() returns n_leaves for a scale and the column leaves for a product, and scale_tree() lists the part leaf with the kind leaf column. Printed output says “Leaves” and “member”.
  • scale_from_leaftable() takes a column called leaf as the leaf column when leaf= is not given, otherwise the finest frame; a column called unit is no longer picked up. The finest frame of scale_example() is item (was unit), which changes its scale_id().
  • Definition files are written with schema version 2: the header field leaf and the table column member. Version 1 files and stores, and objects saved by earlier versions, are still read.
  • backend_scan() and backend_distinct() are no longer exported.
  • write_scale() writes a scale held in meta as a reference, its name and scale_id(), and no longer stops on it.
  • Marked experimental, which means they may change or be removed in a later version: attributes with convert_scale(), products of scales (scale_product(), recast_product() and the product_*() functions), arrays and stored datasets (as_scale_array(), write_scale_dataset(), open_scale_dataset()), distances (scale_distance() and its registry) and reconcile_scale().

New features

  • Labels. A scale carries an optional table of display names keyed by (frame, member, variant): a member may have several named variants, a frame may have none, and a row with member = NA names the frame itself. scale_from_leaftable() takes it as labels=; attach_labels_scale() adds rows and sets the default variant, scale_labels() reads the table and scale_label() looks names up, returning the code where there is no label. join_scale(labels = ) attaches them as "<name>.label". Subsets keep the labels of the members that remain, and write_scale() / read_scale() carry the table.
  • The data link (experimental). bind_scale() records on a table’s code columns which scale and frame they are on; scale_link() reports it and unbind_scale() removes it. A bound column is a character vector of class scale_member (as_scale_member(), is_scale_member()) that keeps the link through subsetting, joins and row binding. recast_scale(), recast(), recast_to_leaves(), recast_from_leaves() and join_scale() take the source frame from the link, stop when the data is bound to another scale, and bind their result; unbound data is handled as before. write_scale_dataset() records the link in the store. The link is lost when a bound column is converted to a factor or a plain character vector, and may change or be removed.
  • scale_id() gives the identity of a scale: its name and a hash of its structure. A link compares the hash alone, so objects with the same structure under different names are interchangeable.
  • scale_tree() lists the parts of a scale or a product as a tree and marks each one fixed (it enters the identity), derived or mutable, naming the function that changes it. str() prints the same tree. scale_payload_parts() is the hook a subclass uses to describe the parts it adds.
  • The classes NestedScale and ScaleProduct are exported, so printing one shows its properties and ?NestedScale documents them.

Compatibility with ‘S7’ 1.0

  • The class of an object is read through S7::S7_class(). ‘S7’ 1.0 keeps it under another attribute, which stopped the label functions and the update of objects saved by earlier versions. ‘S7’ 0.2 is still supported.
  • A test no longer depends on the wording of an ‘S7’ error message, which changed in ‘S7’ 1.0.

nestedscales 0.2.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-03

Breaking changes

  • from and to are now source and target everywhere: the frame arguments of recast_scale(), recast_crosswalk(), recast_to_atoms(), recast_from_atoms(), reconcile_scale(), recast_product() and the navigation functions, the scale arguments and label columns of scale_map(), scale_map_between() and their registry, and the columns of scale_atom_pairs(). recast() takes the scale as scale and the source frame as source. The crosswalk columns n_from and w_from are unchanged. No deprecation aliases.
  • clear_scale_rules(), clear_scale_maps() and clear_scale_distances() take name (and scope where it applies); clear_scale_maps() can now remove named keys.
  • The backend helpers .ms_* are now the backend_* functions: backend_of() (errors on an unsupported input), backend_is_lazy(), backend_schema(), backend_lazy(), backend_pull(), backend_restore() and backend_bind_rows(), plus the new backend_scan() and backend_distinct(). They are documented together under ?backend.

New features

  • Member attributes and aliases. A scale carries two optional long tables keyed by (frame, unit): attributes (a value with its kind, bounds, unit_of_measure, source and note) and aliases (alternative labels). scale_from_leaftable() takes them as attributes= and aliases=; attach_attributes_scale() and attach_aliases_scale() append rows and never overwrite; scale_attributes() reads them, resolved along the hierarchy when a frame is given; scale_aliases() and scale_match() resolve labels exactly and report ambiguity. convert_scale() converts value columns row by row with a resolved attribute: a property is invertible, a factor is one-way (SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS). Both tables survive filter_scale(), [, prune_scale() and clustering, which now keep a subclass as well; scale_payload_collapse() is the hook a subclass with a positional payload overrides for prune_scale(). Objects saved by 0.1.x load unchanged.
  • Definition files. write_scale() and read_scale() exchange a scale as a language-neutral definition: a JSON header with the tables inline, or a <name>.scale/ bundle with Arrow IPC or CSV tables; YAML is accepted as input and as an output option. scale_write_payload(), scale_read_payload() and register_scale_class() let a dimension package store and restore its subclass.
  • Catalogue. register_scale_dir(), list_scale_dirs(), clear_scale_dirs() and scale_catalog() list the definitions shipped by installed packages; read_scale(id) takes a catalogue id.
  • write_scale_dataset() writes _scales/manifest.json; a legacy manifest.yaml is still read. jsonlite is a new import.

Documentation

  • New vignettes: vignette("anatomy") (the object, its tables and what the validator guarantees) and vignette("attributes") (attributes, aliases and conversion). The article Fuels, regions and months on the package site joins a fuel scale, a GeoScale and a Calendar on one table.

nestedscales 0.1.1

  • write_scale_dataset() now falls back to uncompressed Arrow IPC files, with a warning, when the requested compression codec is unavailable in the installed Arrow build.

nestedscales 0.1.0

  • First release. nestedscales is the dimension-agnostic core under timescales and geoscales: their Calendar and Geoscale classes are subclasses of its NestedScale, so every verb below works on calendars and region hierarchies as well as on any other dimension.

Scales

  • A NestedScale is a flat table of atoms plus the ordered frames that group them. Build one with scale_from_leaftable(); read it with scale_frames(), scale_units(), scale_key(), scale_leaftable(), scale_weights(), scale_rank() and scale_atom_level().
  • Frames may cross-cut, and memberships may be partial (NA). The atoms may be the codes of the finest frame or, as for a calendar, combinations of frames held in the key column.
  • scale_family(), scale_ancestry(), scale_nests(), scale_children(), scale_parents(), scale_descendants() and scale_ancestors() navigate the hierarchy; scale_share() and scale_coverage() report weights.
  • Frames need not nest. scale_nests(), scale_crosses() and scale_is_uniform() report the structure a pair of frames (or one frame) actually has, computed from the atoms; the order of frames is the convention the direction-dependent rules (share, residuals, reconciliation) follow.
  • filter_scale() (or x[frame, unit]) and prune_scale() subset and collapse a scale, recording the result’s coverage of the original.
  • scale_class(), scale_is() and their product counterparts stand in for the classes, which are not exported; the package’s surface is its functions.

Conversion

  • recast_scale() converts data between resolutions in either direction with the rules sum, weighted_mean, mean, copy, sd, share and logshare (SCALE_RULES), one per value column if needed. Other columns are kept as identifiers.
  • recast_to_atoms() and recast_from_atoms() are the two halves of the route, and recast between two scales that share atom keys.
  • recast_crosswalk() runs the same engine over a crosswalk built elsewhere, such as timescales’ mapping of one calendar onto another.
  • recast() is the S7 generic that timescales and geoscales extend, so one pipeline can recast time and space in turn.
  • scale_map(x, from, to) returns the crosswalk between two frames of a scale and scale_map_between(from, to) the one between two scales; register_scale_map() / register_scale_map_between() and register_scale_rule() record exact crosswalks and per-column rules. A value column without a rule is an error, never a guess.
  • join_scale() attaches a scale’s labels, coarser frames (attach =), shares and weights to a dataset.
  • Declared residuals (scale_from_leaftable(residuals = ), scale_residuals()) aggregate upward but never receive a share when a coarse value is split. reconcile_scale() compares aggregated data with an independent total and can balance the gap.

Data backends and large data

  • Every verb accepts a data.frame, tibble, data.table, dtplyr table or arrow table/dataset, and returns the same class. Lazy inputs return a query unless collect = TRUE.
  • A target whose sources are only partly present comes back NA; missing_sources = "ignore" aggregates whatever is there instead.
  • diagnostics = controls the checks that scan the data (off by default for lazy inputs); batch = and batch_by = process a job in chunks of identifier values.

Products of scales

  • scale_product() combines several scales (time x space, …) into one multi-index without building its atoms. product_size(), product_keys(), product_frames(), product_weights(), product_coverage() and scale_axes() describe it; product_atoms() realises the grid on request.
  • recast_product() converts any subset of the axes in one call, with rules per value column and axis. join_product() and filter_product() work axis by axis.

Clustering

  • cluster_scale() groups units by their data (k-medoids, hierarchical or k-means) and returns the scale with the clusters as a new frame, so the rest of the package applies to them directly.
  • cluster_contiguous() keeps clusters contiguous in order or in an adjacency graph; cluster_medoids() returns representative units; cluster_sweep() reports cluster quality across a range of k.
  • scale_distance() and its registry (SCALE_DISTANCES, register_scale_distance()) supply level and shape distances.

Arrays and storage

  • as_scale_array() and as_scale_table() convert between long data and a dense array over a scale or product.
  • write_scale_dataset(), open_scale_dataset() and scale_dataset_info() store data as a partitioned Arrow dataset together with its scales, so it reopens ready to recast.

Building a dimension package

  • vignette("nestedscales") introduces the representation and the main functions; the package website includes a roadmap of what the package offers and what is planned.
  • A dimension package defines a NestedScale subclass, as timescales and geoscales do. scale_alias_property() gives an inherited property the dimension’s own name; scale_vocab() puts the dimension’s words in error messages; scale_payload_slice() keeps per-atom data (such as geometry) in step when rows are subset; scale_atom_pairs() lets a dimension generate its atom layer.
  • .ms_backend() and the other .ms_* helpers provide the backend handling to packages built on nestedscales.
